frozen: before the claim and the first launch (the commit that adds this file)

sources.lines: posthoc.json A, B: each arm's minion-rail delta over its pre-launch idle against harts (arm A 600 MHz, arm B 800 MHz; both idles at 600 MHz)

design_note: arm B's harts re-cut so that 3.752 + 0.04049*N matches arm A's -0.343 + 0.02105*N on the minion rail's watts over the common 600 MHz idle, i.e. on the total minion-rail power in the window, which sets the regulator's current at each arm's voltage

V_verdict.model: offrail = a_m*dminion + c_B*[arm B] + R_eff*[((m0 + dminion)/V)^2 - (m0/V0)^2], no other intercept, deltas over each launch's own pre-launch idle, drift_split footing (E77's reading unchanged). c_B is the off-rail part of the 800 MHz operating point's step that a_m does not carry: E77 measured that step post hoc (4.09 W minion, 1.73 W SRAM) and this registers its fit
V_verdict.unit: per pass k: the rung means of arm A pass k and arm B pass k (8 points, 3 coefficients); the unit of replication is the pass; 99% interval = mean +- t(0.995, n-1) * SD/sqrt(n) over passes
V_verdict.PASS: R_eff's 99% interval excludes 0 AND the pooled fit over every rung mean has an rms at least 30% below the same fit without R_eff (E77's rule, unchanged)
V_verdict.NEITHER: the interval excludes 0 but the rms improves by less than 30%: 'R_eff resolved, not a material term'
V_verdict.FAIL: the interval contains 0. A FAIL is a result: the bound B below is then what the run says

expected_from_E77_posthoc_not_a_rule.note: E77's three passes in this form (post hoc); no size or sign of R_eff is frozen as a prediction

B_bound.what: the conduction loss a 21 W minion-rail step adds, in the registered model's total-current form, at the 99% interval's upper edge: R_hi*[((m0_A + 21)/V_A)^2 - (m0_A/V_A)^2], m0_A = arm A's measured idle minion rail (mean of its kept launches), V_A its mean window voltage; as pJ of the 0.875 pJ row, pJ = W x 0.875 / (0.188 x 21). The literal R_hi*(21/V_A)^2 is reported beside it (E77 F2: the literal form is not the registered model's)
B_bound.rule: BOUNDED BELOW THE ROW if the total-current upper edge is under 0.875 pJ; else NOT BOUNDED

C1_e77_posthoc_bound.what: E77's post hoc offset fit, the same form, on fresh data
C1_e77_posthoc_bound.rule: PASS if E120's 99% upper edge is at or under E77's post hoc 0.496 mOhm (0.30 pJ total-current at E77's m0); FAIL otherwise

T1_per_hart_transfer.what: per pass, each arm's least-squares line of rung-mean minion delta against harts; the slope ratio B/A divided by (800/600)*(V_B/V_A)^2 from that pass's mean window voltages
T1_per_hart_transfer.rule: PASS if the 99% interval over passes contains 1 AND the mean is within 5% of 1

S1_step_minion.what: arm B's line intercept minus arm A's, per pass (the 800 MHz operating point on the minion rail with no work)
S1_step_minion.rule: PASS if the mean over passes lies in E77's post hoc 99% interval [3.44, 4.75] W

S2_step_sram.what: arm B's mean SRAM delta minus arm A's, per pass
S2_step_sram.rule: PASS if the mean over passes lies in E77's post hoc 99% interval [1.69, 1.78] W

P2_matching.what: measured minion-rail watts over idle in each rung pair, pooled over passes
P2_matching.rule: PASS if all four pairs are within 5%. The offset fit compares the arms' lines and needs their ranges to overlap, not exact pairs, so a miss does not make the verdict provisional; it is reported

G_one_temperature.what: the arms' mean launch readings (the die mean in the last idle sample)
G_one_temperature.rule: PASS if they differ by at most 1 C (E77: 1.2 C, named)

RING_return.what: the return burst after the restore
RING_return.rule: PASS if the clock reaches 800 MHz in the burst AND the ring dumped after it holds at least one throttle-up entry newer than the dump before it, by service-processor timestamp

K_kernel.what: host kernel 'SP Runtime Error' events between the gate reads and the closing read
K_kernel.rule: reported; E77's 22 were all its own raw-4 residency reads (F1), and E120 reads raw 1-3 only, so any event is named and looked for in the rings
